      "partial_result": "## Verdict: not admissible yet\n\n**Don't freeze the CPU gate yet.** The CPU receipt locks the exact code for every later phase: `check_terminal` requires `record['code'] == context['connected_code']` (`train_siglip2_connected_mlp.py:1516`). So any problem in the mechanics or TRAIN logic counts against the CPU gate too. Fixing it later means rerunning the gate. Two cost-accounting defects are proven from the source. A third problem is arithmetic: the mechanics 300 s and TRAIN 600 s caps can't be met using your own throughput numbers.\n\n## Demonstrated defects (proven from source)\n\n**D1. The \"core\" in the cost ratio isn't the core the recipe froze.**\n- `total_training_core_seconds` is timed from `arm_run` entry (`:1433`) to the end of `qualify_bundle` (`:1476`).\n- That span includes model construction, tamper checks, save/release/restore, bundle export and two public loads. The recipe puts all of those in \"whole\".\n- The gates at `:1579` and `:1665` use this number.\n- Effect: both arms share large fixed costs, which pulls the ratio towards 1. That makes the gate easier to pass, which amounts to relaxing it.\n- **Falsifier:** control core 100 s and candidate core 160 s (true ratio 1.6), plus 200 s shared overhead, gives 360/300 = 1.2, which passes.\n- **Fix:** gate on `sum(r['core_seconds'] for r in rows)` and keep the arm total as a recorded phase. Note that the per-update timer starts after the pre-update `integrity` (`:898`). Decide explicitly whether that check is part of core.\n\n**D2. The in-run \"whole\" ratio is asymmetric** (`:1666`).\n- It divides the candidate's in-process `wall` (timed from `STARTED`, before receipt write and process exit) by the control's systemd `service_seconds`.\n- That favours the candidate by about 1.6%, going by v2: 163.485 s service vs 160.916 s internal.\n- **Fix:** compare against `control_record['wall_seconds']` in-process. The service-vs-service check at `:1580` stays with the parent.\n- No source test covers either ratio. `test_siglip2_connected_mlp.py` has no core/service assertions.\n\n## Projected cap failures (arithmetic from source and receipts, not yet run)\n\n**Hashing cost.** All hashing is uncached by design (`nearest.fingerprint`: \"No stat, version, or tensor-hash cache\").\n- One `integrity()` call hashes the frozen 444 tensors (`:619`, about 1.67 GB), the full 448 (about 1.71 GB), then the full 448 again inside `payload()` (`:683`). That is about 5.1 GB.\n- One `update()` does a pre-update integrity, a post-update `encoder_facts`, a post-update integrity and a payload digest (`:966`). That is about 15 GB of single-threaded SHA-256 per update, roughly 5\u20138 s at 2\u20133 GB/s.\n\n**Compute.** Your own FP32 B16 figures are 45.05 img/s frozen and 42.87 img/s connected. At 128 images per update, that's 364 s (control) and 382 s (candidate) for 128 updates.\n\n**Fixed overhead.** The v2 log reaches `independent_reload` at 92.6 s, and its exit chain takes about 46 s. Call it about 140 s per process.\n\n| Phase | Projection | Cap |\n|---|---|---|\n| Mechanics (34 updates, 4 constructions, tamper checks, 2 public loads \u2248 90 GB extra hashing) | ~450\u2013550 s | 300 s |\n| TRAIN | ~1,200 s+; even with zero hashing ~560\u2013590 s | 600 s |\n| CPU (1 FP32 update of 128 images on 8 threads, unmeasured; ~195 GB hashing) | ~260\u2013400 s, roughly a coin flip | 300 s |\n\n**Fastest falsifier, with no gate attempt:** project each phase from the v2 phase log, the img/s receipt, and one timed `hashlib.sha256` over a 1.7 GB buffer on the DGX.\n\n**Minimal fix that doesn't relax anything:** within one integrity boundary, hash each tensor once and build the frozen-444, full-448 and payload digests from those per-tensor results. Nothing is reused across boundaries and nothing is keyed on pointers or versions. That brings an update down to about 5 GB. **TRAIN at 600 s still has no headroom after that.** So either the root re-freezes the design or cap now, before any run, or the method closes. That isn't a cap rescue, because nothing has been attempted yet.\n\n## Runtime questions (not defects)\n\n- **Memory events:** v2 already peaked at 6.97 GB of 8 GiB with one model. The CPU gate does more file I/O: four 1.7 GB mmap loads and a 1.7 GB bundle write, with `fadvise` only on the reader. Page cache could trip a `memory.events max` event. Record `memory.stat`, and drop pages after the write/fsync.\n- **Processor cache:** `_processor_cache(empty=True)` is process-global. It's fine for this sequential gate, but it would break a library that loads two endpoints at once.\n- **Labelling:** the CPU phase is launched as `--arm control` (`:142`) but actually qualifies the candidate. It's consistent, but the receipts will be confusing to read.\n\n**Checked and OK:**\n- The hardcoded v2 receipt and log SHAs match the evidence copies.\n- The constructor runs under `fork_rng`, so CPU RNG identity holds.\n- Optimizer group order and learning rates are as frozen, and the optimizer binds after the device transfer.\n- Adam step scalars are copied to CPU, and `mapping_absent` runs after release.\n- Every step requires nonzero gradients for all members and before \u2260 after, which rules out a change from weight decay alone.\n- The original-four and same-shape head substitution mutants are both present.\n\n## Scientific matched comparison\n\n1. **Live pixels add no information.** The augmented view's seed is `179081 + train_row` (`pixels_for`). It doesn't depend on step, arm or seed. Layers 0\u201325 and the layer-26 attention are frozen in both arms, so about 96% of TRAIN compute recomputes a fixed function of a fixed input.\n   - **Exact alternative:** cache the layer-26 post-attention residual once (about 1.18 MB per image, about 15 GB FP32 on disk) and train MLP26, the post-norm and the head from it.\n   - **Caveat:** this changes what the \u22641.50 ratio means, so it needs a prospective root decision.\n   - Genuine-pixel trust is already established by the public-loader parity check.\n2. **The candidate trains one objective and serves another.** Training ranks adapted queries against the cached original-encoder gallery. The candidate will mostly fit the teacher regression.
